title: Coordinate correlation and Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and for each $k\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ let $p_k$ be a probability mass function on pairs of signs and let $\rho_k\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that under $p_k$ each sign has expectation zero and the product of the two signs has expectation $\rho_k$. For any function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and any coordinate $i$, the expectation of the product of $f$ evaluated on the first sign vector and the $i$th sign of the second vector, when coordinates are sampled independently according to the $p_k$, equals $\widehat f(\{i\})\rho_i$, where $\widehat f(\{i\})$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the singleton coordinate $\{i\}$.
